title: Anole C ABI configuration
description: The JSON document anole_server_create takes (anole_server_options.config_json). Unknown keys are refused, with the line and column in anole_last_error (token UnknownKey).

executors.description: Executor threads; 0 for one per CPU (cgroup-aware).

errors.description: How the server writes its own error answers (404, 405, the status an error maps to).

format.description: auto: JSON Lines when environment is production, else text. In json, the log callback's msg is the whole record as one JSON object.

service.description: Written as "service" in every JSON record; at most 64 bytes.

console.description: The live console (docs/console.md): a control socket that `anole console` attaches to, and anole_console_open for a terminal in this process.

enabled.description: The control socket; null: on (off under deployment lambda, on Windows, with ANOLE_CONSOLE=0).

name.description: What `anole console <name>` finds the app by; bindings pass the package or module name.

allow_restart.description: /restart and /full-restart; null: on in development, off in production.

log_buffer.description: Bytes of recent log records kept (warnings and errors always, every level while a console shows logs); 0: none.

max_routes.description: Routes with latency numbers of their own; the rest are counted together.

runtime.description: Shown in the console's status line, e.g. "node 22.11.0".

banner.description: Print the startup banner (the anole, the version, the address) to stderr when it is a terminal and log.format resolves to text. Never under systemd. ANOLE_NO_BANNER=1 turns it off.

environment.description: development or production. null: ANOLE_ENV, else production. development: 500 answers name the error (error_detail). See docs/config.md.

deployment.description: What sits in front. null: ANOLE_DEPLOYMENT, else standalone. behind_proxy and platform trust X-Forwarded-* from loopback and private networks; anole_lb expects a PROXY header; platform listens on $PORT. lambda needs Anole 0.4. See docs/config.md.

error_detail.description: A 500 Anole answers for an error with no status of its own names the error. null: on in development.

middleware.description: Native middleware for every route, in order.

databases.description: Databases for anole_db_*, opened at start.

brokers.description: Message brokers for anole_nats_*, opened at start.

jobs.description: The durable job queue for anole_jobs_*.

storage.description: S3-compatible object stores for anole_s3_*, opened at start.

mail.description: Mail servers for anole_smtp_*, opened at start.

lambda.description: AWS Lambda (deployment "lambda"): where invocations come from and how answers go back. Ignored by other deployments. docs/lambda.md.

watches.description: Database changes fed into SSE topics and WebSocket rooms, or read by consumers (anole_watch_*).

runtime_api.description: The Runtime API, host:port; null: AWS_LAMBDA_RUNTIME_API. Set, it also wins over AWS_LAMBDA_HTTP_ENDPOINT.

invoke_mode.description: buffered or response_stream (a Function URL with RESPONSE_STREAM, a REST API with responseTransferMode STREAM); null: ANOLE_LAMBDA_INVOKE_MODE, else buffered.

concurrency.description: Invocations served at once; null: AWS_LAMBDA_MAX_CONCURRENCY (Lambda Managed Instances), else 1.

event_path.description: Where events that are not HTTP requests are POSTed (the event as the JSON body); a 2xx answer's body is the result. null: such events fail the invocation.

base_path.description: Taken off the front of every HTTP event's path (an API Gateway custom domain's base path); null: none.

keep_stage.description: Keep a named stage at the front of an HTTP API path.

context_headers.description: Send the invocation in x-amzn-request-context and x-amzn-lambda-context (a client's own copies are removed either way).

deadline_margin_ms.description: A request still running this long before the invocation's deadline is canceled and answered 504.

idle_reset_ms.description: Close idle outbound and database connections when an invocation arrives this long after the last one ended; null: never.

sigterm.description: Register a no-op Lambda extension so that Lambda sends SIGTERM before it shuts the environment down.

shutdown_timeout_ms.description: The most the shutdown after SIGTERM may take.

flush_timeout_ms.description: The most that sending finished spans may hold up the next invocation.

name.description: What anole_s3_find looks it up by: unique, 1-255 bytes.

timeout_ms.description: A bound on every call that has no timeout_ms of its own. 0: none.

errors.description: What status each class of database error becomes (anole.db.ErrorMap): a class name to the status it answers with.

attempts.description: Attempts in all, the first included.

attempt_timeout_ms.description: A bound on each attempt; 0: none.

consecutive_failures.description: Open after this many failures in a row; 0: not this rule.

failure_ratio.description: Open when failures / calls reaches this over window_ms, once min_calls calls are in it; 0: not this rule.

open_ms.description: The first open period; it doubles after each failed probe.

half_open_calls.description: Calls let through at once while half-open.

breaker.description: A circuit breaker: after repeated connection failures calls fail fast with ANOLE_E_DB, class UNAVAILABLE, error_code "circuit_open" and http_status 503. null: none. Ignored for SQLite.

anyOf.description: "https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com", "http://127.0.0.1:9000". Null: AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, else AWS.
Null: AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, else the provider's.
The default bucket; null: S3_BUCKET.
Keys: both or neither (neither takes the AWS credential chain).

payload_signing.description: auto hashes the body over plain HTTP only.

anyOf.description: The same as PEM text.

min_throughput.description: Bytes per second a call that moves a body is given on top of timeout_ms.

anyOf.description: A body of known length up to this size goes up as one PUT; null: part_size.

concurrency.description: Parts of one upload in flight at once, 1..16.

upload_memory.description: Part buffers of every upload together.

max_object_bytes.description: A whole-body get larger than this fails with ANOLE_E_TOOBIG.

anyOf.description: Unique, 1-255 bytes, no ':'. Requests carry it (`listener` in the record). Default "http-<port>" / "https-<port>".

address.description: "127.0.0.1" (this machine), "" (every interface, IPv6 and IPv4), "0.0.0.0", "::". null: the deployment's ("127.0.0.1"; "" for anole_lb and platform).

port.description: 0 picks a free port (anole_server_listener). null: 8080, or $PORT under platform.

anyOf.description: A unix domain socket at this path instead of address and port.

http2.description: HTTP/2: h2 by ALPN over TLS, h2c (prior knowledge) in cleartext.

http3.description: HTTP/3 over UDP on a TLS listener (one per server); its port follows the listeners' in anole_server_listener (udp_port).

proxy_protocol.description: Connections start with a PROXY protocol header. null: on under anole_lb, else off.

proxy_protocol_from.description: With proxy_protocol: the proxies allowed to send one (addresses or CIDR networks); empty: proxy.trusted when set, else any peer.

tcp.description: Raw TCP instead of HTTP (needs a port or unix; not with http3).

udp.description: UDP instead of HTTP (needs a port; not with tls, unix or proxy_protocol).

NetFraming.description: How input is cut into messages: exactly one of lines, length, varint. Left out: bytes as they arrive.

max.description: A line longer than this (without its end) closes the connection.

crlf.description: anole_net_write with ANOLE_NET_F_FRAME ends the line with "\r\n".

includes_header.description: The length counts its own bytes.

max.description: A frame longer than this closes the connection.
A frame longer than this closes the connection.

NetTcp.description: A raw TCP listener: connections and their data go to the consumer as events (ANOLE_EV_NET_*), not HTTP.

handler.description: Carried in the listener's records (handler_id); any number the consumer picks.

half_open.description: After the peer ends its side the connection stays open for writing until the consumer ends it (ANOLE_EV_NET_END).

keepalive_ms.description: TCP keep-alive probes after this much silence; null: off.

handshake_timeout_ms.description: The PROXY header and the TLS handshake, together; null: the request timeout.

idle_timeout_ms.description: No input for this long closes the connection; null: never.

lifetime_ms.description: The longest a connection may stay open; null: no limit.

write_timeout_ms.description: A flush the peer does not take for this long closes the connection; null: none.

write_high_water.description: Past this many queued bytes anole_net_write answers ANOLE_BUSY.

write_max.description: Past this many it takes nothing (ANOLE_E_AGAIN).

read_window.description: The read buffer of each burst.

read_ahead.description: Bytes of one connection posted and not yet polled, at most.

max_connections.description: Open connections on this listener, at most; null: the server's limit alone.

log_connections.description: One access-log line per closed connection.

NetUdp.description: A raw UDP listener: datagrams go to the consumer in batches (ANOLE_EV_NET_DATAGRAMS). No TLS, unix socket or PROXY header.

sockets.description: SO_REUSEPORT sockets (Linux), each on an executor; null: one per executor.

max_datagram.description: The largest datagram taken; a larger one is dropped and counted.

send_queue.description: Bytes waiting to go out per socket.

anyOf.description: PEM file, read at start and by anole_server_reload_tls with both arguments empty.
PEM text, instead of files.

self_signed.description: A fresh self-signed certificate for localhost (development).

anyOf.description: ALPN protocols in order; default h2, http/1.1.

client_auth.description: Mutual TLS: "request" asks for a client certificate and checks one that is sent; "require" refuses a client without one. Also over HTTP/3. Requests carry the certificate (ANOLE_REQ_PEER_CERT).

anyOf.description: PEM file of the CAs client certificates must chain to (with client_auth request or require).
The same CAs as PEM text, instead of client_ca_file.
A directory of PEM files for the CAs client certificates must chain to, instead of client_ca_file.

client_ca_system.description: The system's trust store as the CAs client certificates must chain to.

Tls.description: Exactly one of cert_file + key_file, cert_pem + key_pem, self_signed.

body_max.description: The largest request body, inline or streamed: past it, 413.

max_head_size.description: The request line and headers; larger is 431. 1024 to 1048576.

inline_body_max.description: Bodies up to this come inline in the request record; larger ones are read with anole_req_read.

max_inflight.description: Requests handed to consumers and not yet answered, per executor; past it, 503.

queue.description: Events waiting for a consumer, per executor; 0 = twice max_inflight.

stream_high_water.description: Bytes waiting in a streamed response before anole_req_stream_write answers ANOLE_BUSY.

ws_high_water.description: Bytes waiting on a WebSocket before anole_ws_send answers ANOLE_BUSY.

ws_max_message.description: The largest WebSocket message, in or out (after inflating).

max_connections.description: Open connections at most; 0 follows the open-file limit.

anyOf.description: Requests per keep-alive connection; null: no limit.

db_result_max.description: The largest database answer (its record's bytes); past it, ANOLE_E_TOOBIG.

sse_max_event.description: The largest event anole_sse_publish and anole_sse_send take.

anyOf.description: A consumer request's default deadline: 504 from Anole after it. Null: none.
The request head on HTTP/1.x (Slowloris). Null: request_ms alone.
A write the peer does not take for this long ends the response. Once a stream or file body has started it replaces the request deadline. Null: none.
An idle keep-alive connection is closed after this. Null: never.
An idle HTTP/1.1 connection gives up its task after this. Null or 0: never parks.
How long a drain waits for requests in flight. Null: for all of them.

rewake_ms.description: Ring a consumer's doorbell again when its events stay unpolled this long (a lost wake); 0 never.

anyOf.description: The UDP address; null: the TLS listener's.
The UDP port; null: the TLS listener's.

validate_address.description: Make every new client prove its address with a Retry first.

alt_svc.description: Advertise HTTP/3 with Alt-Svc on the TLS listener's responses.

early_data.description: Take 0-RTT from resuming clients (replayable: only safe methods run before the handshake completes).

prefer_v2.description: Move clients that offer QUIC v2 to it.

anyOf.description: UDP sockets on Linux; null: one per executor.

inline_no_wait.description: Run no_wait requests that arrive whole on the endpoint task.

trusted.description: The proxies in front: addresses, CIDR networks or "loopback", "private", "link_local". Only their X-Forwarded-* is read; the client is the rightmost X-Forwarded-For address not among them. null: ANOLE_PROXY_TRUSTED, else the deployment's (loopback and private for behind_proxy, anole_lb, platform; none for standalone). []: none.

trusted_hops.description: A fixed number of proxies instead of the walk: the client is the trusted_hops-th X-Forwarded-For address from the right; with trusted, only from a trusted peer. 0: the walk (or nothing, with no trusted).

trust_forwarded_proto.description: From a trusted proxy: the last X-Forwarded-Proto value says whether the request is secure.

trust_forwarded_host.description: From a trusted proxy: the last X-Forwarded-Host value is the request's host (only when every proxy in front sets it).

Proxy.description: Trust in proxies in front of the server.

require_host.description: HTTP/1.1 without exactly one Host is 400.

keep_buffers.description: Keep a connection's request buffers between requests.

write_buffer_size.description: Bytes buffered while a response is written; at least 1.

date.description: Send a Date header on every response.

anyOf.description: The Content-Type of a buffered body whose handler set none, by name ("text", "json", ...); null: none.

max_header_count.description: Most headers a response can carry.

brotli_quality.description: Brotli's quality, 0 to 11, for responses compressed as br.

max_concurrent_streams.description: Streams a client may have open at once.

stream_window.description: Request body bytes a client may send on a stream before the handler reads them.

stream_window_reading.description: The stream's window from the handler's first read of the body.

tunnel_window.description: The window (and body buffer) of a tunnel stream, a WebSocket over HTTP/2 (extended CONNECT): one fixed window, no raise.

reading_window_budget.description: The most memory the raised windows of one connection's streams take at once.

connection_window.description: Request body bytes in flight across all streams of a connection.

max_header_list_size.description: The decoded size of a request's header block.

stream_reset_burst.description: RST_STREAM a client may send in a burst before the connection is closed.

max_continuations.description: CONTINUATION frames allowed after one HEADERS.

refused_stream_burst.description: Streams the server may refuse in a burst before the connection is closed.

enable_connect_protocol.description: Advertise SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL (RFC 8441): WebSockets over HTTP/2. Off by default: browsers then open WebSockets over HTTP/1.1, which costs about half the CPU per message.

inline_no_wait.description: Run no_wait requests that arrive whole on the connection's reader.

Http2.description: HTTP/2 settings, for h2c and h2 over TLS.

Middleware.description: One native middleware, as an object with a single key naming it.

exclude.description: Paths not logged: exact, or a prefix ending in '*'.

compress.description: zstd, Brotli or gzip, as the client accepts.

anyOf.description: The provider's JWK Set URL, fetched and refreshed.

audience.description: Required in the token's aud. Required with jwks_url (a provider's keys also sign tokens for its other clients), unless allow_any_audience.

allow_any_audience.description: With jwks_url and no audience: only for keys that sign for this application alone.

scopes.description: Each must be in the scope claim; 403 otherwise.

jwt.description: Exactly one of jwks_url and jwks; jwks_url needs audience (or allow_any_audience). The verified claims reach the consumer as JSON (`claims`).

key.description: "ip" (the client's address) or "header:<name>" (the header's raw value, unverified: only for a header a trusted proxy sets to a verified identity, since a client that varies it gets a fresh limit each time).

webhook_verify.description: Checks an incoming webhook's signature before the handler runs (400 when wrong) and drops duplicate deliveries (200 for one already processed, 409 while it is being processed).

anyOf.description: One or more (rotation). standard: whsec_<base64> (v1) or whpk_<base64> (v1a public key); stripe: the whsec_ text as it is; github, slack, hmac: the shared secret.
An environment variable holding one secret, or several separated by spaces.

tolerance_ms.description: The timestamp window, both directions (standard, stripe, slack).

on_store_error.description: When the duplicate store fails: answer 503, or run the handler without it.

prefix.description: Stripped from the header value first ("sha256=").

id_header.description: A header with the delivery's id, for duplicates.

checks.description: Readiness flags: each starts not ready, so /readyz answers 503 naming it until the consumer calls anole_server_set_ready.

listener.description: Serve both routes only on the listener of this name (404 on the others).

anyOf.description: GET, POST, ...; left out: every method.
A consumer's route id: requests go to a consumer.
This route's request deadline (handler routes, and websocket routes with "accept": "consumer": the decision's; at most 16 distinct values per server).

no_wait.description: Handler and respond routes run on the HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 reader when they can (no task per request); false gives each request a task.

Route.description: Exactly one of handler, respond, static, websocket, webtransport, sse; handler and a websocket with "accept": "consumer" may go together.

headers.description: Not Connection or Transfer-Encoding: the server writes those.

handler.description: The consumer's route id for this endpoint's events.

accept.description: Who answers the handshake: "auto" (Anole: origins and subprotocols; the consumer hears ANOLE_EV_WS_OPEN) or "consumer" (ANOLE_EV_WS_UPGRADE, answered with anole_ws_accept or refused like any request). With "consumer" the route may also carry "handler": plain requests of the path go to it.

subprotocols.description: "auto" only: the subprotocols this endpoint speaks, most preferred first; the first the client offered is selected and echoed (ANOLE_EV_WS_OPEN says which).

origins.description: Pages of other origins that may open the socket, besides the request's own host ("https://app.example.com"); "*" for any. A browser handshake from any other origin gets 403.

handler.description: The consumer's route id for this endpoint's events.

close_on_drain.description: Close each session (code 0) when the server drains, right after ANOLE_EV_WT_DRAIN; false leaves that to the consumer (until timeouts.shutdown_ms).

origins.description: Pages of other origins that may open a session, besides the request's own host; "*" for any. A browser request from any other origin gets 403.

datagram_queue.description: Datagrams a session holds for sending; past it the oldest is dropped (counted in anole_server_stats).

WebTransport.description: A WebTransport endpoint (draft-02, over HTTP/3): sessions, streams and datagrams go to a consumer. Needs a listener with http3; takes no method.

name.description: What anole_db_find looks it up by: unique, 1-255 bytes.

cache.description: Bounds of the answers kept for queries with cache_ttl_ms, over every executor.

timeout_ms.description: A bound on every query that has no timeout_ms of its own, in a request or not; past it the statement is interrupted (ANOLE_E_TIMEOUT). 0: none.

consecutive_failures.description: Open after this many failures in a row; 0: not this rule.

failure_ratio.description: Open when failures / calls reaches this over window_ms, once min_calls calls are in it; 0: not this rule.

open_ms.description: The first open period; it doubles after each failed probe.

half_open_calls.description: Calls let through at once while half-open.

breaker.description: A circuit breaker: after repeated connection failures calls fail fast with ANOLE_E_DB, class UNAVAILABLE, error_code "circuit_open" and http_status 503. null: none. Ignored for SQLite.

attempts.description: Attempts in all, the first included.

attempt_timeout_ms.description: A bound on each attempt; 0: none.

retry.description: What queries with ANOLE_DB_F_RETRY are retried with, on a transient failure (the server unreachable, a connection lost). Ignored for SQLite and MongoDB.

errors.description: What status each class of database error becomes (anole.db.ErrorMap): a class name to the status it answers with.

Database.description: A database for anole_db_*: exactly one of sqlite, postgres, redis and mongodb.

uri.description: Take a path starting with "file:" as a SQLite URI.

anyOf.description: Read-only connections beside the writer; left out: one per executor, at most 8; 0: everything on the writer.

busy_timeout_ms.description: How long a statement waits for a lock another process holds.

pragmas.description: Run on every connection as it opens.

anyOf.description: SQL run once at start, before the listeners open: a schema.

ping_timeout_ms.description: What /readyz waits for the database's answer.

anyOf.description: postgres://user:password@host:port/database?params. Null: DATABASE_URL, else libpq's variables (PGHOST, PGUSER...).
libpq's sslmode. Null: the URL's, else PGSSLMODE, else verify-full for a server on another host and prefer on this machine.

Connections in all, split between the executors. Null: the URL's pool_max_conns, else twice the executors, at least 4.

acquire_timeout_ms.description: How long a query waits for a connection when all are busy.

connect_timeout_ms.description: How long opening a connection may take; 0: no limit.

max_lifetime_ms.description: Connections older than this are closed; 0: no limit.

idle_timeout_ms.description: Connections idle this long are closed; 0: no limit.

connect_at_start.description: Open a connection per executor at start, and fail the start if that fails.

reset_session.description: What happens to a connection's session when a query gives it back: "auto" resets it when what the query ran may have changed it, "always" on every release, "off" never.

anyOf.description: SQL run once at start, before the listeners open: a schema.

rediss://: a PEM file of the CA certificates the server's certificate is checked against. Null: the URL's ssl_ca_certs, else the system's store.
The same as PEM text.
Connections in all, split between the executors. Null: ten per executor.

acquire_timeout_ms.description: How long a command waits for a connection when all are busy.

connect_timeout_ms.description: How long opening a connection may take; 0: no limit.

idle_timeout_ms.description: Connections idle this long are closed; 0: no limit.

insecure_skip_verify.description: TLS without checking the server's certificate. Refused with a CA and with a URL that verifies.

ping_timeout_ms.description: What /readyz waits for the server's answer.

Redis.description: A Redis or Valkey server (anole.redis; docs/database.md).

anyOf.description: A mongodb:// connection string; its options win over the fields below. mongodb+srv:// is not supported yet (list the hosts with mongodb://). Null: MONGODB_URI, else mongodb://localhost:27017.
The database operations name no other for. Null: the URL's path, else "test".

The same as PEM text.
Connections at most, split between the executors (maxPoolSize). Left out: 100.

acquire_timeout_ms.description: How long an operation waits for a pooled connection.

server_selection_timeout_ms.description: How long an operation waits for a server it can use (a primary).

connect_timeout_ms.description: TCP connect and TLS handshake; 0: no limit.

insecure_skip_verify.description: TLS without checking the server's certificate. Refused with a CA and with a URL that verifies.

ping_timeout_ms.description: What /readyz waits for the server's answer.

idle_timeout_ms.description: Idle connections older than this are closed; 0: never.

heartbeat_ms.description: Between two checks of a server.

retry_reads.description: Retry a read once after a network error or a primary change.

retry_writes.description: Retry a single-document write once, likewise.

connect_at_start.description: Select a server and open a connection per executor at start, and fail the start if that fails.

ttl_ms.description: When the answer's Cache-Control does not say.

authenticated.description: Also keep answers to requests with credentials.

Grpc.description: gRPC services whose methods the consumer implements (-Dgrpc). Anole serves gRPC over HTTP/2, gRPC-Web, Connect and JSON transcoding, with framing, compression, deadlines, limits and health; messages reach the consumer as protobuf bytes (ANOLE_EV_GRPC_CALL).

descriptor_set.description: The services' descriptors: a serialized google.protobuf.FileDescriptorSet with its imports (protoc --include_imports --descriptor_set_out, buf build -o), base64. With descriptors Anole knows each method's call mode and serves JSON (Connect JSON, gRPC-Web JSON, google.api.http transcoding) by converting to and from protobuf; without them every service lists its methods and only protobuf is served.

descriptor_set_file.description: The same, as the path of the file (read by anole_server_create). One of descriptor_set and descriptor_set_file.

health.description: Serve grpc.health.v1.Health: the server ("") and every service here SERVING until anole_grpc_health_set says otherwise, NOT_SERVING once the server drains.

handler.description: The consumer's route id for this service's calls (anole_grpc_call_event.route_id).

methods.description: The methods served, in the order of their method_id. Left out: all of the service's, in the descriptors' order (needs descriptors).

max_message_size.description: The largest request message, after inflating; a larger one ends the call with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. A consumer's poll buffer must hold a call record with one.

max_received_bytes.description: Request message bytes one call takes in all (each counted at its size plus 64); past it, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.

read_timeout_ms.description: How long a request message may take once it started arriving; 0 for no limit but the deadline.

max_call_duration_ms.description: The longest a call may run, capping the client's deadline; 0 for none.

response_compression.description: When response messages are gzipped: when the request's were (mirror), whenever the client accepts gzip (accepted), never.

read_ahead.description: Request messages of a client- or bidirectional-streaming call delivered before the consumer asks for more (anole_grpc_read).

transcode.description: REST routes for the methods annotated with google.api.http (needs descriptors).

no_wait.description: Unary and server-streaming calls that arrive whole over HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 run with no task (detached), as no_wait routes do.

middleware.description: After the global ones; runs for the service's gRPC paths and its transcoded routes, as a route's middleware does.

name.description: The method's name, as in the .proto ("SayHello").

kind.description: The call mode; needed without descriptors, else checked against them.

no_side_effects.description: Also serve the method as Connect GET (unary only). Default: the descriptors' idempotency_level = NO_SIDE_EFFECTS.

heartbeat_ms.description: A comment line to every subscriber idle this long; null: none.

retry_ms.description: Sent as retry: at the start of each stream; null: the browser's default.

replay.description: Null: no ids, no replay, no gap events.

max_queued_bytes.description: Bytes waiting for one subscriber (each event counts 64 more).

on_full.description: close: a subscriber that does not keep up is sent what is queued and its stream ends (the browser reconnects and resumes from the replay); drop: the event is skipped for it.

close_after_ms.description: close: a sender stuck this long on a full subscriber aborts its stream.

leave_grace_ms.description: How long a write under way may finish before it is canceled.

gap_event.description: The gap event's name; null sends no gap events.

drain_retry.description: The retry spread at the drain; null: streams just end.

total_bytes.description: Every topic together; the globally oldest event goes first.

max_per_resume.description: One resume replays at most this many events, else it is a gap.

topics.description: Topics a subscriber joins; {name} is the path's parameter name.

last.description: Without Last-Event-ID: the newest this-many events of each topic.

handler.description: A consumer route id: subscribe requests become ANOLE_EV_SSE_SUBSCRIBE, and the subscriber joins topics plus those of anole_sse_accept.

database.description: A databases entry of the matching kind.

Watch.description: Exactly one of postgres, redis, redis_stream and mongodb.

patterns.description: PSUBSCRIBE patterns (room:*); at least one channel or pattern.

start.description: "new", "all" or {"after": ["id", ...]}, one entry ID per key.

pipeline.description: An Extended JSON array of stages after $changeStream.

sse.description: A topic (a template: {channel}, {op}, {data.<field>}, and for MongoDB {db}, {collection}, {key}).

WatchTo.description: Exactly one of sse and ws.

name.description: What anole_nats_find and anole_kafka_find look it up by: unique, 1-255 bytes.

extra.description: Any other keys of the stream configuration the server takes.
Any other keys of the consumer configuration the server takes.

nats.description: A NATS server or cluster (exactly one of the kind keys).

brokers.description: host:port entries. Null: KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, else KAFKA_URL, else localhost:9092.

tls.description: TLS to the brokers; any ca or client certificate key turns it on too.

kafka.description: A Kafka cluster (exactly one of the kind keys).

timeout_ms.description: A bound on requests and JetStream calls that have no timeout_ms of their own. 0: none.

errors.description: What status each class of database error becomes (anole.db.ErrorMap): a class name to the status it answers with.

attempts.description: Attempts in all, the first included.

attempt_timeout_ms.description: A bound on each attempt; 0: none.

retry.description: What queries with ANOLE_DB_F_RETRY are retried with, on a transient failure (the server unreachable, a connection lost). Ignored for SQLite and MongoDB.

store.description: A databases[].name (SQLite, PostgreSQL or Redis), or "memory" (lost on restart).

lease_ms.description: How long a claimed job is held without a heartbeat.

poll_ms.description: Staging, idle claims and rescue checks.

notify.description: LISTEN/NOTIFY (PostgreSQL) or pub/sub (Redis) wakes; off behind PgBouncer transaction pooling.

kinds.description: Kinds known by name: their defaults for anole_jobs_enqueue.

keep.description: How long finished jobs are kept before the leader prunes them.

leader.description: Which instance runs schedules and maintenance.

drain_ms.description: How long a server drain lets running jobs finish before they are put back.

cron.description: Schedules: each enqueues a job of kind, or runs a statement.

schedule.description: Five fields, or six with seconds first; @daily and the like; @every 90s.

tz.description: An IANA name, "UTC" or an offset; null: UTC.

kind.description: The kind to enqueue; exactly one of kind and sql.

sql.description: A statement run on a configured database (SQLite or PostgreSQL) at each tick.

Webhooks.description: Webhooks out (-Dwebhooks; needs "jobs"): endpoints, signed deliveries run as jobs, retries with backoff and the delivery log. Endpoint management and replay go through anole_jobs_admin; anole_webhooks_publish sends events.

queue.description: The jobs queue deliveries run on.

concurrency.description: Deliveries at once in this process.

multiplier.description: Ceilings 5 s, 25 s, 2 min, 10 min, 52 min, 4.3 h, 21.7 h, 24 h.

consecutive_failures.description: Open after this many failures in a row; 0: not this rule.

failure_ratio.description: Open when failures / calls reaches this over window_ms, once min_calls calls are in it; 0: not this rule.

open_ms.description: The first open period; it doubles after each failed probe.

half_open_calls.description: Calls let through at once while half-open.

breaker.description: A circuit breaker per endpoint origin (scheme, host and port): while open, deliveries wait without an attempt. null: none.

allow_private_addresses.description: Deliver to loopback and private addresses. null: allowed in development, refused in production.

require_https.description: Refuse http:// endpoints. null: not required in development, required in production.

response_kept.description: Bytes of an endpoint's answer kept in the log.

disable_after_ms.description: An endpoint whose deliveries have all failed for this long is disabled.

secrets_key_env.description: The environment variable holding the 32-byte base64 key that encrypts stored secrets; "" for none.

name.description: What anole_smtp_find looks it up by: unique, 1-255 bytes.

url.description: smtp://user:pass@host:587 (STARTTLS), smtps://user:pass@host:465, smtp://127.0.0.1:1025?tls=none. Null: SMTP_URL, else Mailpit's smtp://127.0.0.1:1025 (not in production).

tls_mode.description: auto: smtps:// is implicit TLS, smtp:// to a public host requires STARTTLS, to loopback it uses STARTTLS when offered.

helo_name.description: The EHLO name. Null: the host name.

max_connections.description: Connections in all, split between executors. Null: 2 per executor.

max_messages_per_connection.description: A connection QUITs after this many messages.

idle_timeout_ms.description: Idle connections are closed after this; 0: never.

min_throughput.description: Bytes per second a send may take at the least, added to the timeout for the message's size.

max_message_bytes.description: Refused before connecting when the encoded message is larger.

readiness.description: Register a readiness check (/readyz): connect, EHLO, QUIT, cached 30 s.

timeout_ms.description: A bound on every send that has no timeout_ms of its own, plus the message's size at min_throughput; 0: none.

consecutive_failures.description: Open after this many failures in a row; 0: not this rule.

failure_ratio.description: Open when failures / calls reaches this over window_ms, once min_calls calls are in it; 0: not this rule.

open_ms.description: The first open period; it doubles after each failed probe.

half_open_calls.description: Calls let through at once while half-open.

breaker.description: A circuit breaker: after repeated connection failures sends fail fast with ANOLE_E_SERVICE, class UNAVAILABLE, error_code "circuit_open" and http_status 503. null: none.

attempts.description: Attempts in all, the first included.

attempt_timeout_ms.description: A bound on each attempt; 0: none.

retry.description: What sends with ANOLE_SMTP_F_RETRY are retried with, on a failure before the final "." (a failure after it is never retried).

errors.description: What status each class of database error becomes (anole.db.ErrorMap): a class name to the status it answers with.
